title: §20-001: Password Hashing with Argon2 & Salt Rounds
description: Multiple-choice practice questions and deep runtime verification for §20-001 (Password Hashing with Argon2 & Salt Rounds).

cards.concept: Password Hashing with Argon2 & Salt Rounds: Password Hashing: Argon2id vs Bcrypt
cards.question: Why are memory-hard algorithms like Argon2id or bcrypt required for password hashing rather than fast algorithms like SHA-256?

options.text: SHA-256 cannot hash strings longer than 32 characters.
SHA-256 is designed to be extremely fast, allowing GPU/ASIC hardware to compute billions of guesses per second; Argon2id requires substantial memory and compute, thwarting brute-force cracking.
Argon2id produces reversible encryption keys.
bcrypt does not require salt generation.

cards.explanation: Fast hash functions allow attackers to test billions of password candidates per second. Memory-hard algorithms (Argon2id) force high memory and CPU time per hash, rendering offline cracking infeasible.
cards.pitfall: Setting work factors (cost/salt rounds) too low makes hashes vulnerable; setting them too high blocks the event loop with synchronous crypto.
cards.citation: OWASP Password Storage Cheat Sheet / RFC 9106 Argon2

cards.concept: Password Hashing with Argon2 & Salt Rounds: JWT Algorithm Confusion Attacks
cards.question: How does the 'algorithm confusion' vulnerability compromise JSON Web Token (JWT) verification, and how is it prevented in Node.js?

options.text: Attackers alter the token expiration timestamp.

Attackers forge a token signed with the public RSA key using HMAC-SHA256, exploiting verifiers that accept any algorithm in the token header; defend by explicitly locking `algorithms: ['RS256']` in `jwt.verify()`.
Attackers decode Base64 tokens to read the payload.
Attackers replay revoked tokens to different endpoints.

cards.explanation: If jwt.verify() does not specify an algorithms whitelist, an attacker can change 'RS256' to 'HS256' and sign the token using the server's public key (which is publicly accessible).
cards.pitfall: Storing sensitive authentication JWTs in browser localStorage exposes them to instant exfiltration via Cross-Site Scripting (XSS).
cards.citation: RFC 7519 / Auth0: Critical Vulnerabilities in JSON Web Token Libraries
